baseline_models.focus_anchor: The repeated د ع و frames the contrast between تدعونني and أدعوكم, while the lam-clause and ila-phrase give the two calls opposed directions.
baseline_models.mechanism: Calling inclines an addressee by speech. Their call aims to produce concealment of God and allocation of a partner; the speaker's counter-call directs them instead toward invincible power joined to repeated forgiveness.

activation_trace.role: Calling and verbal inclination supply the directional force shared by both halves of the contrast.
Concealment or denial of truth supplies the first intended effect of their call.
Shared participation supplies the second intended effect: introducing another into what belongs to God.
Power and inviolability make the speaker's destination resistant to the rival call.
Covering sin while protecting its bearer makes forgiveness the restorative end of the counter-call.

changed_reading.before: The speaker contrasts two religious appeals.
changed_reading.after: The ayah stages two directional speech systems: one tries to produce concealment and shared divinity, while the other redirects its hearers toward unassailable, restorative divine agency.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The object of أشرك is qualified by ما ليس لي به علم.
baseline_models.mechanism: Partnership is treated as an allocation of participation that requires a knowable basis. The negated state of knowledge, reinforced by the branch image of a distinguishing mark, blocks assignment of any divine share to the proposed other.

activation_trace.role: Participation held between parties supplies the allocation that the speaker refuses to make.
Present-state negation removes any existing epistemic basis for the proposed partnership.
Recognition and disclosed knowledge supply the missing warrant.
A distinguishing mark that guides to its referent makes the absence of any identifying evidence concrete.
Worship and the worshipped establish the exclusive relation into which an unsupported participant would be inserted.

changed_reading.before: The speaker merely says that he does not know the alleged partner.
changed_reading.after: The speaker enacts epistemic non-participation: without disclosure or a distinguishing sign, he will not allocate a share in worship by assertion alone.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: أكفر and الغفار place two cover-images on opposite sides of the verse.
baseline_models.mechanism: The same material operation is ethically reversed. Kufr covers or suppresses God, truth, or benefaction; the Ghaffar covers sin in order to preserve the sinner from its consequence. Aziz adds the power that makes the preserving cover effective.

activation_trace.role: Literal covering supplies the suppressive operation demanded by the hostile invitation.
A cover that guards what it encloses supplies the protective reversal.
Covering sin and shielding its bearer specifies the beneficial object and result of the second cover.
Invincible strength makes the protective covering more than concealment.

changed_reading.before: Disbelief and forgiveness are separate theological opposites.
changed_reading.after: The invitation is a contest between two coverings: a human act that obscures the divine and a divine act that covers culpability so the human can be preserved.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus ending recombines the surah's opening names. Aziz returns from the descent formula, focal no-knowledge stands against Alim, and Ghaffar intensifies the opening Ghafir. The speaker's counter-call therefore routes his audience back to the revealed source already characterized by knowledge, power, and pardon.

activation_trace.role: The speaker's negated recognition forms the epistemic gap answered by the opening divine name.
Invincible power is the repeated name that ties the focal destination to the source of the book.
Repeated forgiveness turns the destination into a return to the surah's initial offer of pardon.
Power and inviolability characterize the source from which the book descends.
Complete recognition at the surah's opening contrasts with the speaker's refusal to claim unsupported knowledge.
Forgiving sin supplies the opening offer that the focal title Ghaffar renews and intensifies.

structural_cues: 40:2 closes the descent formula with Al-Aziz Al-Alim, and 40:3 opens with Ghafir al-dhanb.
40:42 places negated ilm immediately before the destination Al-Aziz Al-Ghaffar.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the recurring names and their positions; I infer that the focal counter-call deliberately returns hearers to the surah's opening source. A live alternative is ordinary thematic reuse of divine names rather than a designed return.

changed_reading.before: Al-Aziz Al-Ghaffar are fitting attributes appended to the speaker's appeal.
changed_reading.after: The names act as a retrieval address: the believer sends his audience back to the knowledgeable, powerful, forgiving source announced at the surah's opening.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier call-scenes expose a conditional switch: being called to faith produces disbelief, and invoking God alone produces disbelief, while introducing partnership produces assent. The focus does not merely list two errors; تدعونني لأكفر وأشرك names the output that this established call-program tries to reproduce in the speaker.

activation_trace.role: Verbal inclination anchors the present attempt to move the speaker into the earlier response pattern.
Denial of truth is the first programmed response.
Making a partner for God is the condition under which the earlier audience becomes receptive.
Repeated denial brackets the recalled moment when they were called to faith.
The earlier call toward faith supplies the rejected input to the behavioral switch.
Invocation makes the audience's opposed responses directly comparable.
Divine uniqueness without partner supplies the condition that they reject.
Denial is the response activated by exclusive invocation.
Adding a partner supplies the condition under which they instead assent.

structural_cues: 40:10 recalls that a call to faith was answered with disbelief.
40:12 pairs disbelief when God alone is invoked with belief when partnership is introduced.
40:42 repeats the same sequence as the intended effects of their call.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated conditional sequence; I infer that the current invitation attempts to install that response pattern in the believer. A live alternative is that 40:10-12 describes a broader class rather than the immediate addressees alone.

changed_reading.before: The addressees advocate disbelief and polytheism as two related propositions.
changed_reading.after: Their invitation operates like a loyalty switch: exclusive divine address is to trigger refusal, while shared divinity is to trigger acceptance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The believer first asks to be followed along a rightly directed path, then names the rival calls' terminal states as rescue and fire. The focus unfolds those destinations into their operating commitments: kufr and shirk are the road into fire, while orientation to Aziz and Ghaffar is the road of extraction and rescue.

activation_trace.role: The two calls provide the directional operator whose routes and endpoints the context reveals.
Following behind someone turns the believer's speech into offered leadership along a route.
Gentle indication toward road and truth supplies the manner of his counter-leadership.
An extended traversable road gives the invitation a spatial and processual form.
A straight route away from error specifies the quality of the believer's proposed path.
The immediately preceding mirrored calls explicitly connect the two speakers to opposite destinations.
Rescue by separation supplies the extraction achieved by the believer's route.
Kindled fire supplies the consuming terminal state of the rival route.

structural_cues: 40:38 offers followership, guidance, a path, and rectitude in one compact sequence.
40:39-40 insert the temporary world, settled abode, action, and recompense between route and destination.
40:41 contrasts rescue and fire; 40:42 immediately replaces those outcomes with the commitments and divine names that lead to them.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies route vocabulary and explicit destinations; I infer that the focal grammatical complements are stages in those routes rather than detached doctrines. A live alternative is that 40:41 only summarizes the stakes while 40:42 independently specifies belief content.

changed_reading.before: The verse contrasts the doctrinal content of two invitations.
changed_reading.after: Each invitation is a traversable causal route: following one installs kufr and shirk and reaches fire, while following the other separates the hearer toward rescue under Aziz and Ghaffar.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later call-scenes test invitations by whether their endpoint can sustain a claim and answer. The proposed other has no call or claim in either world, all return to God, calls made in the fire go astray, and God alone explicitly pairs 'call Me' with 'I answer.' The focal contrast thus distinguishes a dead-end call from a reciprocal address.

activation_trace.role: The mirrored verbal calls anchor the question of which addressed destination can answer.
Calling is repeated while the invited object is denied any effective call in either world.
An asserted right or claim keeps open the alternative that the denied da'wah is standing rather than audible response.
Present-state negation removes effective call or valid claim from the proposed partner.
Return to the proper destination closes the failed rival circuit at God.
Calls from within the fire supply a failed communication circuit whose speech reaches no relief.
The divine imperative to call supplies the open side of a reciprocal address.
Answering speech completes the response circuit absent from the rival object.

structural_cues: 40:43 immediately denies da'wah to what they invite the believer toward and states the common return to God.
40:49-50 stage a request to call for relief whose ensuing calls are declared lost.
40:60 directly joins the imperative 'call Me' to the promise 'I answer you.'
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies negated da'wah, return, failed calls, and explicit answer; I infer that efficacy links these scenes and differentiates the focal destinations. A live alternative is that da'wah in 40:43 means a valid claim or intercession rather than response capacity.

changed_reading.before: Both sides possess formally comparable invitations.
changed_reading.after: The symmetry is only verbal: their invitation terminates at an object with no sustainable call or claim, while the believer's invitation enters a divine call-and-answer circuit.

context_deltas.mechanism: After inviting them to Aziz and Ghaffar, the believer does not seize control; he transfers his affair to God, and protection from their plot follows. Divine power and protective covering become an enacted sequence of delegation and warding rather than titles used to overpower the audience.

activation_trace.role: Invincible strength supplies the agency to which the threatened speaker can entrust his affair.
A cover that guards what it encloses supplies the protective shape later made visible.
Returning one's affair to another in reliance transfers control from the speaker to the divine endpoint he names.
Warding off harm supplies the concrete protective result of that delegation.

structural_cues: 40:44 follows the invitation by entrusting the speaker's affair to God.
40:45 begins with the resulting divine protection from the evils of the plot.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies immediate delegation followed by protection; I infer that this sequence operationalizes Aziz and the protective cover-image of Ghaffar. A live alternative is that the outcome vindicates trust narratively without unpacking the two names individually.

changed_reading.before: The believer invokes divine might and forgiveness as persuasive attributes.
changed_reading.after: He models their operation: relinquished control enters invincible agency, and that agency places a preserving barrier between him and the plot.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah repeatedly describes disputation without a compelling warrant, delays forced knowledge until consequences arrive, and finally depicts people exulting in the knowledge locally possessed by them despite clear proofs. Against that pattern, the focal 'I have no knowledge of it' is disciplined restraint: the believer refuses to manufacture participation where no authority or sign has arrived.

activation_trace.role: Allocating shared participation is the act withheld pending warrant.
Negation marks a presently absent epistemic basis rather than an invented certainty.
A mark that reveals and guides to its referent supplies the evidence the alleged partner lacks.
Compelling proof supplies the authority explicitly absent from the disputants' case.
The repeated absence of compelling proof confirms a stable epistemic defect rather than a one-time omission.
Future recognition supplies knowledge imposed after rejection, too late to ground the earlier claim responsibly.
Exultant arrogance turns local knowledge into a closed affective possession.
Nearness and presence make their knowledge something merely 'with them,' set against what the messengers bring.
Their possessed recognition supplies the overconfident counterpart to the believer's candid epistemic limit.

structural_cues: 40:35 and 40:56 repeat the formula of arguing about God's signs without a sultan that came to the disputants.
40:70 postpones their knowing until after rejection of the book and messengers.
40:83 juxtaposes clear proofs with delight in the knowledge already 'with them.'
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies absent authority, delayed knowing, and self-satisfaction in possessed knowledge; I infer that the focal admission models responsible non-assignment. A live alternative is that it refers narrowly to not knowing any identity or reality for the proposed partners.

changed_reading.before: The believer answers a false claim by admitting personal ignorance.
changed_reading.after: His admission is an epistemic discipline opposed to arrogant pseudo-possession: absent authoritative disclosure, no participant may be inserted into divine worship.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the hunting-snare branch of ش ر ك rather than its ordinary theological branch. It remains anchored in the focal أشرك and gains visible support when later shirk is followed by collars, linked chains, dragging, and the disappearance of what had been called. Downstream prose should present it only as an exploratory material analogy, not as the lexical definition of shirk in 40:42.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focal أشرك can retain the branch-distant image of entering a hunter's snare while still denoting the demanded partnership.

activation_trace.role: A hunter's snare supplies the exploratory image of participation as self-entanglement.
A collar binding a limb materializes the restraint latent in the snare image.
Connected links turn the claimed relation of partnership into a binding relation.
Dragging and extension supply the forced motion that follows capture.
The later interrogation about shirk reconnects the chain scene to the focal partnership root.
Their denial that they had called anything leaves the captives bound after the supposed partner vanishes.

changed_reading.before: Shirk is an abstract attribution of a divine share to another.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the invitation to shirk is an invitation into a relational snare: its claimed links disappear as partners but persist as the captive's bonds.

strongest_changes: The focal closing names return the believer's audience to the surah's opening source of knowledge, power, and forgiveness.
The earlier call-scenes reveal a conditional loyalty switch in which exclusive invocation triggers disbelief and partnership triggers assent.
The immediate route and destination sequence turns the two calls into causal paths toward rescue or fire.
The later negated, failed, and answered calls expose an asymmetry between a dead-end invitation and reciprocal divine address.
The speaker's lack of knowledge becomes disciplined refusal to assign divine participation without authoritative disclosure.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah context made the focus operate simultaneously as a return to the opening names, the center of a repeated call-response pattern, a route choice in a threatened public argument, and an epistemic refusal that later self-satisfied knowledge throws into relief.
remaining_uncertainties: دعوة in 40:43 may foreground a valid claim or intercession more than response capacity.
The opposed-covering model is lexically anchored but its shared material image may be associative rather than an intended local contrast.
The snare-and-chain activation is deliberately exploratory and should not displace the ordinary partnership sense of ش ر ك.
The narrative sequence supports causal readings, but some links may be thematic juxtaposition rather than encoded causation.
